messages:
jess: Heads-up — we need a rollout plan for the EU model hotpatch (small param fix). Goal: no latency regression, no quality regression, minimize cost blips. Can we sketch feature-flag/canary/A-B + fallback matrix?

anita: +1. proposal: two-phase canary with a shadow validation step. rough flow: shadow -> 1% internal -> 5% prod canary -> 20% regional -> full. each step gated by telemetry checks.

ryan: add: warmup prefix caching before routing live traffic. KV-cache cold starts will skew p95 if we jump straight to prod. recommend synthetic warmup traffic from canary nodes.

alec: ops notes: we should reserve a tiny dedicated pool for canary so autoscaling churn doesn't affect baseline. also pre-create fallback slots (smaller quantized variant) to pop in if latency or OOMs spike.

jess: good — what flags and naming? need per-tenant opt-in for Acme/BigCorp who asked for deterministic outputs too.

anita: flag naming suggestion (short & discoverable):
```
ff/model/hotpatch/eu: global switch
ff/model/hotpatch/eu.canary_pct: integer (0-100)
ff/model/hotpatch/eu.optin_tenants: list
```
Use featureflag service to gate by region + tenant. Canary percentages: 1 -> 5 -> 20. A/B test variation: route X% to patched model and keep Y% on baseline for quality delta.

ryan: metrics to gate on: p95_latency (tokens/sec), 99th_mem_pressure, error_rate (500s), cost_per_kilo_tokens, quality_delta_on_promptset (we have a 200-prompt smoke set). threshold examples: p95_latency +5% allowed, error_rate <0.1%, quality_delta <1% drop.

alec: ops runbook snippet to switch fallback quickly:
```
# fast rollback steps
1) set ff/model/hotpatch/eu = false
2) set routing weight to baseline model: route.set_weight(patched=0, baseline=100)
3) scale down canary pool
4) notify #incidents and customer-ops
```
Make sure the flag API call is <1s and monitored.

jess: customer opt-ins: we'll create per-tenant opt-in list. for enterprise customers we keep them pinned until they request removal. note: need legal signoff if data path changes.

ops-bot: checklist: shadow validation ✓, canary pool reserved ✓, smoke promptset evaluated ✓, dashboards created (model-hotpatch-eu) — pending launch.

anita: acceptance criteria before moving 5% -> 20%:
- no increase in p95 beyond 5% for 30m after warmup
- error_rate <0.1% for 60m
- quality_delta <= 1% on smoke set for 60m
- memory headroom stable (no OOMs)
If any fail, auto-degrade to baseline and trigger postmortem.

ryan: one more: run a quick A/B eval measuring hallucination rate on 100 prompts (holdout) — if hallucination delta >0.5% fail.

deploy-bot: CANARY STARTED: 1% traffic to model-hotpatch-eu in eu-west-1 at 1715010000.

jess: thanks — schedule 30m immediate check and 2h follow-up. @anita please own the telemetry gate, @alec own the rollback automation, @ryan own warmup script. I'll notify customer-ops about opt-in config.

anita: will post dashboards and a short playbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hotpatch-rollout (internal).

alec: I'll add an automated SLA guard that flips ff/model/hotpatch/eu false if any of the hard gates fire and will emit an incident notice.

ryan: warmup snippet (run from canary nodes):
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS https://canary.local/generate -d @sample_prompt.json >/dev/null; done
```
This will populate KV cache and warm kernels.

jess: perfect. we'll reconvene after the 30m check. thanks team :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: NOTE: canary pool reserved nodes = 4, baseline pool unaffected. logs streaming to logs-hotpatch-eu.*

ops-bot: post-launch action: if any tenant reports regressions, set ff/model/hotpatch/eu.optin_tenants = ["acme-corp"] to isolate.

jess: assigned and closing loop for now — move to #shiproom at +20% window.
